Tides are the rhythmic rising and falling of the ocean's surface, a grand planetary dance driven primarily by the gravitational pull of the moon. Although the sun is vastly larger, the moon exerts a stronger tidal influence simply because it is much closer to Earth. This gravitational force does not merely pull on the water; it stretches the entire planet slightly, creating a bulge of water on the side facing the moon where the pull is strongest. Simultaneously, a second bulge forms on the opposite side of the Earth. This counter-intuitive phenomenon occurs because the solid Earth is pulled toward the moon more strongly than the water on the far side, effectively leaving that distant water behind in a relative outward swell.

As the Earth rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours, different coastlines sweep through these two stationary bulges. When a location passes through a bulge, high tide occurs, lifting the water level significantly. Conversely, when that same spot rotates into the areas between the bulges, the water recedes to create low tide. This rotation means that most coastal regions experience two high tides and two low tides roughly every day, though the exact timing shifts slightly later each day as the moon continues its own orbit around our planet.

The sun also plays a crucial supporting role in this celestial mechanics. When the sun, moon, and Earth align during full and new moons, their combined gravitational forces create exceptionally high and low tides known as spring tides. In contrast, when the sun and moon form a right angle relative to Earth during the quarter phases, their forces partially cancel each other out, resulting in weaker tidal ranges called neap tides. Beyond simple gravity, the shape of the coastline, the depth of the ocean floor, and local weather patterns can amplify or dampen these effects, making the tide at any specific beach a unique interaction between cosmic forces and local geography. Ultimately, tides represent a constant, visible reminder of our intimate gravitational connection to the heavens above.
